To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the extent of grain processing is a function of the grain particle size and the extent of grain cooking, and 2) the extent of digestion of starch is a function of grain processing and the rate of grain passage through the digestive tract, which is determined by rumen volume per unit weight and the rate of outflow of rumen contents.

1) grain processing increases starch digestion in the small intestine and 2) the extent of increase is greater for corn than for barley and wheat, 3) grain processing has no effect on the rate of starch digestion in the large intestine, 4) grain processing increases the extent of starch digestion in both the rumen and large intestine, 5) grain processing increases total tract starch digestion, 6) the extent of the increase is greater for barley and wheat than for corn, 7
1) the digestible energy value of corn grain is 1.2 Mcal/kg DM, and 2) processing corn grain with steam improves the digestible energy of corn grain from 1.2 to 1.5 Mcal/kg DM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of grain processing and quality on Holstein steer performance.
the impact of grain processing and quality on Holstein steer performance.
the impact of grain processing on the performance of Holstein steers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
grain processing is important in feedlot diets.
grain processing has a positive impact on the performance of Holstein steers, particularly on the digestibility of starch.
grain processing improves the efficiency of utilization of starch and other nutrients in the rumen and small intestine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

grain processing affects ruminal digestion of grain starch and the extent to which the starch is digested, but does not affect the efficiency of utilization of the energy from starch that is digested.
the digestibility of starch in the rumen is greater when grains are processed than when they are not processed.

starch digestion and utilization in ruminants is a complex function of 1) grain processing, 2) grain source, 3) grain particle size, 4) grain physical properties, 5) rumen pH, and 6) rumen microbial population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
grain processing is an effective way of increasing the efficiency of energy use by feedlot cattle.
grain processing has a greater impact on digestibility in Holstein steers than in beef breeds.
the digestible energy content of cereal grains can be increased by grain processing and the digestibility of starch can be increased without affecting the digestibility of other nutrients.
